description: A PHP static analysis tool for finding errors and security vulnerabilities in PHP applications

latest_release.body:
<!-- Release notes generated using configuration in .github/release.yml at 81bda61675df22fc4e5e1ceab1c33f4c61a4830b -->

## What's Changed
### Fixes
* Narrow arrays of the same keys that are identical to an array of overlapping item types by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12707
* fix(memoization): keep a memoized call narrowed in the initialization pass by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13120
* Keep a mixed variable mixed after a ternary that narrows it by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12725
* Fix: @method of a used trait or parent class overriding a declared method by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13546
* Fix parser caching for project paths containing vendor by @MohannadElemary in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13491
* fix(types): isset narrows optional properties of object shapes by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13409
* fix(static-properties): forget a static property after a call to a method that assigns it #10705 by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13262
* fix(conditional): a value is never of the type never in a conditional return type by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13433
* Don't let the conditions of the caller reach a method analysed inline by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12732
* fix(docblock): reject the removed self-accessing/self-mutating callables with params by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12776
* fix(types): '0' is a non-empty-lowercase-string by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12832
* fix(templates): keep the key of a list when its template types are replaced by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12837
* fix(array_pop): an optional last item of a list may leave the previous one popped by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12825
* fix(alter): replace a whole union return type by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12876
* Name the element of psalm.xml a config path error comes from by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12616
* fix(types): validate refined stringable arguments by @1cbyc in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13472
* fix(functions): bind the template of a conditional return type whatever the casing of the call by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12656
* Report an int range offset that partly fits the keys of an array as possibly invalid by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12710
* fix(shapes): keep an optional key of an unsealed shape through isset and the join of branches by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12646
* Resolve self of a trait method's return type to the class using the trait (#4047) by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12742
* fix(calls): name the callable in TooFewArguments and TooManyArguments by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12637
* fix(callable): parse and print by-reference parameters of callable types by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13290
* fix(and): a variable assigned in the right operand of && may keep its earlier type by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13361
* fix(closures): the self of a closure parameter called in a trait is the using class by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13301
* ctype checks of an expression of the implied type are not redundant (#12431) by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12748
* fix(psalter): don't remove the others when fixing an unused property by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12840
* fix(stubs): exec() output is list<string> for an empty array by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12844
* fix(types): cases() on a bare enum-string is a call on UnitEnum by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12908
* feat(array_intersect_key): limit the result keys to the keys of sealed shapes by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12774
* fix

detail.readme:
Psalm

[![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/v/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/dt/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm coverage](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/coverage.svg?)](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm level](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/level.svg?)](https://psalm.dev/) Psalm is a static analysis tool for finding errors in PHP applications. [Join the official Psalm news channel](https://t.me/psalmphp) and the Psalm community on [Telegram](https://t.me/psalmphp_community) and [Discord](https://discord.gg/RwH8rEpxt9)! ## Installation To get started, check out the [installation guide](docs/running_psalm/installation.md). ## Live Demo You can play around with Psalm [on its website](https://psalm.dev/). ## Documentation Documentation is available on [Psalm’s website](https://psalm.dev/docs), generated from the [docs](https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/blob/master/docs) folder. ## Support Psalm development You can support Psalm development by requesting a support contract from [Daniil Gentili](https://daniil.it), the only active maintainer of Psalm. Support contracts can cover full integration of Psalm into existing codebases, support for Psalm issues and development of additional Psalm features. See [here »](https://daniil.it) for info, pricing and contact information. ## Interested in contributing? Have a look at [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Who made this Built by Matt Brown ([@muglug](https://github.com/muglug)). Maintained by Daniil Gentili ([@danog](https://github.com/danog)), Alies Lapatsin ([@alies-dev](https://github.com/alies-dev)) and Orklah ([@orklah](https://github.com/orklah)). Former maintainer: Bruce Weirdan ([@weirdan](https://github.com/weirdan)). The engineering team at [Vimeo](https://github.com/vimeo) have provided a lot encouragement, especially [@nbeliard](https://github.com/nbeliard), [@erunion](https://github.com/erunion) and [@nickyr](https://github.com/nickyr).
